title: Hosted GPU overload: eviction & traffic-shaping postmortem and remediation playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2025-02-17 22:06 UTC we observed a sustained hosted-api capacity event that caused GPU pool saturation, large request queues (up to 18x normal queue depth), and progressive request throttling for lower-tier customers. Symptoms were: sudden surge in client traffic from a single self-serve tenant + a regression in the admission controller (credit expiry window increased due to a config rollout) + autoscaler cooldown/hysteresis preventing rapid priming. The combined effect prevented the system from shedding nonessential work and from priming GPU instances quickly, leading to prolonged elevated latency and 12% elevation in 5xx for impacted customers.

Root cause analysis: three primary contributing factors were identified:
1) Admission control regression: a config change that lengthened token-credit expiry allowed aggressive clients to hoard credits and prevented fair-share draining. The change was introduced in runtime PR #6123 and rolled to canary on 2025-02-16.
2) Autoscaling hysteresis + priming race: autoscaler cooldown was set to 6 minutes; pool priming (instance startup + model load) averaged 4.5 minutes, which combined with the admission regression produced a window where additional capacity was not requested early enough.
3) Insufficient queue prioritization: all requests were queued FIFO which amplified head-of-line blocking by long-running generations and prevented fast, high-priority control traffic (health checks, admin operations) from reducing global pressure.

Impact: ~18% of requests to the hosted inference endpoint experienced latency > 3s during the window; higher-tier customers were protected by priority routing but several self-serve customers saw degraded performance. No data loss or customer data leakage was detected.

Decisions made:
- Roll back the admission-control config that increased credit expiry (rolled back at 2025-02-17 23:10 UTC).
- Short-term: implement emergency queue drain by preempting long-running low-priority requests and enabling short-term burst capacity for customer-tiered pools.
- Medium-term: implement per-tenant soft-limits + priority-aware admission and a faster autoscale priming path (warm-standby flow).

Playbook / Action items (owner — ETA — status):
- Fix admission controller bug in runtime: disallow credit expiry > 30s and add unit tests covering credit decay edge cases. Owner: Marco Rivera — ETA: 2025-02-28 — status: In Progress.
- Implement priority-aware queueing: add token for 'customer_tier' and preemption hooks to drop/evict lowest-priority request after 90s in queue. Owner: Saanvi Rao — ETA: 2025-03-07 — status: Planned.
- Autoscaler tuning & priming optimization: reduce cooldown to 90s for high-variance pools and add parallel model prefetch during instance bootstrap. Owner: Priyanka Singh — ETA: 2025-03-04 — status: In Progress.
- Canary and chaos test: add a synthetic traffic test that simulates a single-tenant traffic surge (60x baseline) exercising admission + scaling. Owner: Chaos Eng — ETA: 2025-03-12 — status: Planned.
- Runbook update: document emergency queue-drain steps, dashboard links, and PagerDuty escalation steps. Owner: Marco Rivera — ETA: 2025-02-25 — status: Done.
- Observability: new alerts for (a) queue-depth per-pool > 10x baseline (b) credit-imbalance per-tenant > 5x expected (c) autoscale request-to-provision lag > 2m. Owner: Elena Gomez — ETA: 2025-02-26 — status: In Progress.
- Customer communications: post-incident email + status page update with timeline and mitigation steps. Owner: Customer Success (Liam Chen) — ETA: 2025-02-20 — status: Done.

Testing & verification plan: run integration test harness with prioritized queueing in staging; run canary with progressive ramp of traffic from 1x to 50x; measure median tail latency, 5xx rates, and time-to-primed-capacity. Add regression coverage to CI for admission-controller config validation.

Related docs and artifacts: PRs, dashboards, and incident notes are linked below in attachments. This ticket will coordinate cross-team follow-ups and produce a GDoc postmortem for leadership review.
